description: AstroNova is a team passionate about technology, space, and using NASA data to solve real-world problems. 🚀🌎 We welcome members interested in coding, web development, data analysis, Earth science, agriculture, UI/UX design, and creative problem-solving. Beginners are welcome too! What matters most is being motivated to learn, collaborate, and build something meaningful together.
summary: Field Shift es una plataforma web de agricultura de precisión desarrollada para empoderar a pequeños y medianos productores, enfocando su validación inicial en la región de Mao, Valverde, República Dominicana. Utiliza datos satelitales en tiempo real de NASA POWER y cálculos de evapotranspiración FAO-56 para el análisis del clima y el suelo. Además, integra Google Gemini para realizar diagnósticos visuales de los cultivos mediante inteligencia artificial, ofreciendo recomendaciones inmediatas y estrategias de rotación basadas en las prioridades del agricultor, democratizando así el acceso a tecnología agrícola de alto nivel.
details:
What it does & How it works Field Shift is an advanced decision-support web platform designed to help farmers adapt to changing climate realities. It translates complex aerospace data into actionable agricultural strategies. The user selects their exact plot of land on an interactive map. The system then processes real-time Earth observations, historical climate patterns, and local soil moisture data. By combining this data with the farmer's specific priorities (e.g., "adapting to heat" or "reducing water usage"), the platform generates highly accurate crop rotation strategies to strengthen soil health.

Benefits & Intended Impact Our primary goal is to democratize precision agriculture. Small and medium-sized farmers often lose crops due to unpredictable weather and a lack of access to scientific tools. By focusing our initial prototype and validation on the agricultural region of Mao, Valverde (Dominican Republic), Field Shift proves that we can bridge the gap between global space tech and local farming. The intended impact is to increase crop yield, prevent soil degradation, and provide a scalable tool that can be used by any farmer around the world.

Tools, Coding Languages & Technologies

Frontend & Architecture: Developed as a Single Page Application (SPA) using Next.js and Tailwind CSS for a seamless, fast, and responsive user experience.

Space Agency Data: We integrated the NASA POWER API to retrieve surface meteorology and solar energy data, alongside the FAO-56 model for precise evapotranspiration calculations.

Artificial Intelligence: We implemented the Google Gemini API to power a computer vision diagnostic tool, allowing farmers to upload photos of their crops for instant disease detection crossed with current weather conditions.

Mapping: Leaflet with Sentinel-2 satellite imagery integrations.

Creativity & Factors Considered The critical factor our team considered was the "digital divide." Terabytes of scientific data are useless if they overwhelm the end-user. Therefore, our most creative approach was implementing a "Progressive Disclosure" UX/UI design. We designed a dark-mode, premium, yet highly intuitive interface that presents simple answers first (like temperature alerts and clear rotation choices) while keeping the rigorous scientific methodology and detailed data accessible in expandable panels. This ensures the tool is scientifically robust for agronomists, yet completely accessible to everyday farmers.
